task.title: Record validated commits only after the Git object batch passes its integrity gate
task.description:
Deferred from PR #36 (WB-01KYT6XA289VV2QNGTXZG9S31H, "Bound full history validation time and peak memory growth").

Streaming the object batch changed when the batch's integrity gate runs relative to when results are persisted.

internal/gitstore/history.go:246-250 calls stream.End for the last task - which reaches historyFold.end and then Cache.Record (internal/historyvalidation/validator.go:274) - and only afterwards calls batch.Finish(). Finish (internal/gitstore/batchstream.go:119-139) is what confirms Git exited 0 and left no trailing output, and its own comment at batchstream.go:116-118 states that trailing output "makes every record in it untrustworthy".

Before the rewrite the entire batch, including both of those checks, completed inside readTaskHeadsPartialBatch before Validate evaluated or recorded anything, so a batch that failed its gate recorded nothing. Now a batch that Finish rejects has already written N tasks to validation.sqlite with status 'valid', and the next non-full `workbook validate` treats them as cache hits without re-reading them.

The reviewer could not construct a reachable failure, and neither could this pass: validateBatchSnapshot cross-checks each response's commit object ID against the requested head (internal/gitstore/batch.go:172-174), so any stream misalignment is caught per commit, and a nonzero Git exit mid-stream surfaces as an unexpected EOF inside readBatchObjects before End runs. So this is a weakened invariant with no demonstrated exploit, not a live bug.

Two acceptable resolutions: either defer the Cache.Record calls until after Finish succeeds (for example by buffering completions per batch, which costs O(tasks) small records rather than O(commits)), or soften the batchstream.go:116-118 comment so the stated invariant matches the actual ordering.

Related and equally narrow: a nonzero Git exit that survives to Finish now surfaces as CategoryOperational "git cat-file --batch failed" where the pre-PR path returned CategoryCorruptData "cannot read task tips". Worth deciding deliberately if the error taxonomy is user-visible.

Deferred because there is no reachable failure path today and the fix trades against the memory bound the PR was built to establish; it deserves its own design pass rather than a late edit under review.
